body.statement:
The following two conclusions hold.

First, for every sequence in the covariate-design class \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{PSRR}}^{x}\), use \(N_x\), \((W^x_{n,m})\), and \(T_n^x\) from \(\mathrm{lem{:}covariate\mbox{-}path\mbox{-}characteristics\mbox{-}and\mbox{-}clock}\), and set
\[
 \bar D_n^x(t)=D_n\!\left(W^x_{n,\min\{\lfloor nt\rfloor,T_n^x\}}\right),
 \qquad
 A_n^x=\sum_{m=0}^{T_n^x-1}\mathbf 1\{W^x_{n,m+1}\ne W^x_{n,m}\}.
\]
Along even \(n\ge N_x\), jointly in \(D([0,\infty),\mathbb R^k)\times[0,\infty)\),
\[
 (\bar D_n^x,T_n^x/n)\Rightarrow(D_{\cdot\wedge H},H),
 \qquad \frac{T_n^x-A_n^x}{n}\longrightarrow_{\Pr}0. \tag{14}
\]
Here, before \(H=\inf\{t\ge0:\|D_t\|^2\le a\}\),
\[
 dD_t=\left(-4D_t-\frac{8\gamma D_t}{\|D_t\|^2}\right)dt+\sqrt8\,dB_t,
 \qquad D_0=G\sim\mathcal N_k(0,I_k), \tag{15}
\]
and \(H<\infty\) almost surely.  If \(R_0=\|D_0\|^2=r\), \(b=k/2-\gamma\), and \(\lambda>0\), then the proposal-time first-entry law has the computable transform
\[
 \mathbb E_r(e^{-\lambda H})=
 \begin{cases}
 1,&r\le a,\\[2mm]
 \displaystyle\frac{U(\lambda/8,b,r/2)}{U(\lambda/8,b,a/2)},&r>a,
 \end{cases} \tag{16}
\]
where, for \(A>0\) and \(x>0\),
\[
 U(A,b,x)=\frac1{\Gamma(A)}\int_0^\infty e^{-xt}t^{A-1}(1+t)^{b-A-1}\,dt. \tag{17}
\]
For \(\lambda=0\), (16) is understood as one.  Under the Gaussian initialization, with \(F_{\chi_k^2}\) the chi-square distribution function,
\[
 \mathbb E(e^{-\lambda H})=F_{\chi_k^2}(a)+
 \frac{\displaystyle\int_a^\infty U(\lambda/8,b,r/2)r^{k/2-1}e^{-r/2}\,dr}
 {\displaystyle 2^{k/2}\Gamma(k/2)U(\lambda/8,b,a/2)}. \tag{18}
\]
For every \(r>a\) and \(\lambda>0\), the transform in (16) is strictly increasing in \(\gamma\); thus finite tuning changes the proposal-time search law.  Equations (14) and the rejection estimate show that the accepted-switch clock used in the published presentation and the all-proposal clock differ by \(o_{\Pr}(n)\).

Second, for every sequence in the outcome-inference subclass \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{PSRR}}\), along the retained even outcome tail \(n\ge N_0\), jointly in \(D([0,\infty),\mathbb R^{k+1})\times[0,\infty)\),
\[
 \bigl(\bar Z_n,T_n/n\bigr)\Rightarrow
 \left(\bigl((D_{t\wedge H}^{\mathsf T},E_{t\wedge H})^{\mathsf T}\bigr)_{t\ge0},H\right), \tag{19}
\]
where (15) holds and \(E\) is the independent stationary solution of \(dE_t=-4E_tdt+\sqrt8\,dB'_t\), \(E_0\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\).  This is the unique weak solution of the stopped system in \(\mathrm{def{:}limit\mbox{-}system}\).  No projected Markov property is assumed in either clause.
body.proof_tex:
We prove the covariate and joint clauses separately.

For a sequence in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{PSRR}}^x\), use the smooth extension furnished by
\(\mathrm{lem{:}covariate\mbox{-}path\mbox{-}characteristics\mbox{-}and\mbox{-}clock}\), and let
\(X_n(t)=D_n(W^x_{n,\lfloor nt\rfloor})\) denote its proposal-clock interpolation before absorption.  The extension agrees with original PSRR through \(T_n^x\).  Its limiting drift and covariance are
\[
 \beta_\phi(d)=-4d-8\gamma\phi'(\|d\|^2)d,
 \qquad c_\phi=8I_k. \tag{28}
\]
The clock conversion in that lemma already expresses (28) on the original treated--control proposal scale.

We first prove compact containment.  Stop at the first exit \(\sigma_{n,R}\) from the radius-\(R\) ball.  Sum the compactly stopped second-moment drift inequality in the characteristic lemma through
\(\lfloor nL\rfloor\wedge\sigma_{n,R}\).  The complete-randomization covariance identity gives
\(\mathbb E\|X_n(0)\|^2=k\), and the maximal score bound makes the exit overshoot \(O(n^{-1/2})\).  Markov's inequality therefore gives
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{\sup_{t\le L}\|X_n(t)\|>R\right\}
 \le\frac{k+CL+o(1)}{(R-Cn^{-1/2})^2}. \tag{29}
\]
The right-hand side is uniformly small after \(R\to\infty\).

On a fixed ball, the predictable drift rate and quadratic-variation rate are bounded, and every jump is \(O(n^{-1/2})\).  If \(\sigma_n\le L\) is a stopping time and \(\delta_n\downarrow0\), the predictable finite-variation increment over
\([\sigma_n,\sigma_n+\delta_n]\) is \(O(\delta_n+n^{-1})\), while conditional Chebyshev applied to the martingale increment yields
\[
 \Pr\{\|M_n(\sigma_n+\delta_n)-M_n(\sigma_n)\|>\eta\}
 \le C\eta^{-2}(\delta_n+n^{-1}). \tag{30}
\]
Equations (29)--(30) give tightness in \(D([0,L],\mathbb R^k)\); the vanishing maximal jump implies that every subsequential limit is continuous.

For \(f\in C_c^3(\mathbb R^k)\), Taylor's theorem and the \(O(n^{-1/2})\) jump bound give, before compact exit,
\[
 \begin{split}
 \mathbb E\{f(X_{n,(m+1)/n})-f(X_{n,m/n})\mid\mathcal F^x_{n,m}\}
 &=\nabla f(X_{n,m/n})^{\mathsf T}
   \mathbb E(\Delta D^x_{n,m}\mid\mathcal F^x_{n,m})\\
 &\quad+\frac12\nabla^2f(X_{n,m/n}):
 \mathbb E(\Delta D^x_{n,m}\Delta D^{x\mathsf T}_{n,m}
 \mid\mathcal F^x_{n,m})+O(n^{-3/2}). \tag{31}
 \end{split}
\]
The trajectory-uniform characteristic bounds make the sum through \(nL\) of the difference between (31) and
\(n^{-1}\mathcal L_\phi f(X_{n,m/n})\) converge to zero in probability, where
\[
 \mathcal L_\phi f(d)
 =\beta_\phi(d)^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(d)
  +4\operatorname{tr}\{\nabla^2f(d)\}. \tag{32}
\]
Compact stopping makes the errors bounded, so truncation upgrades this convergence to \(L^1\).  Passing the conditional martingale identity to any subsequential limit shows that, for \(0\le s<t\) and every bounded continuous path functional \(Q\) measurable through time \(s\),
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[
 Q\left\{f(X_t)-f(X_s)-\int_s^t\mathcal L_\phi f(X_u)\,du\right\}
 \right]=0. \tag{33}
\]
Thus each limit solves the martingale problem for (32).

Because \(\phi\) is constant near zero, smooth on the transition annulus, and equal to the logarithm away from zero, the map
\(d\mapsto\phi'(\|d\|^2)d\) is globally Lipschitz.  Picard iteration therefore constructs a strong solution of the stochastic differential equation with coefficients (28).  If two solutions use the same Brownian motion, the Lipschitz bound, the elementary inequality
\(\sup_{u\le t}\|\int_0^u g_v\,dv\|^2\le t\int_0^t\|g_v\|^2\,dv\), and Gronwall's inequality give
\[
 \mathbb E\sup_{u\le t}\|X_u-X'_u\|^2
 \le C\int_0^t\mathbb E\sup_{v\le u}\|X_v-X'_v\|^2\,du=0. \tag{34}
\]
Hence the martingale problem in (33) has a unique law.  The initial-score CLT identifies \(X_0=G\), so tightness and uniqueness identify convergence of the whole extended process.

Before first entry, \(\phi'(\|D_t\|^2)=1/\|D_t\|^2\).  Applying Ito's formula to \(R_t=\|D_t\|^2\) gives
\[
 dR_t=8(k-2\gamma-R_t)\,dt+\sqrt{32R_t}\,d\beta_t,
 \qquad R_t>a, \tag{35}
\]
with generator
\[
 \mathcal L_Rg(r)=16r g''(r)+8(k-2\gamma-r)g'(r). \tag{36}
\]
A scale derivative is
\(s'(r)=e^{r/2}r^{\gamma-k/2}\), since direct differentiation gives \(\mathcal L_Rs=0\).  Let
\(H_a=\inf\{t:R_t\le a\}\) and \(H_M=\inf\{t:R_t\ge M\}\).
Optional stopping of the bounded martingale
\(s(R_{t\wedge H_a\wedge H_M})\) gives, for \(a<r<M\),
\[
 \Pr_r(H_M<H_a)=\frac{s(r)-s(a)}{s(M)-s(a)}. \tag{37}
\]
The denominator tends to infinity with \(M\).  On every compact interval \([a,M]\), the diffusion coefficient in (35) is bounded away from zero.  Solving the linear boundary-value equation
\(\mathcal L_Rg=-1\), \(g(a)=g(M)=0\), gives a bounded nonnegative \(C^2\) solution; Ito's formula then shows that the exit time from \((a,M)\) has finite expectation.  Letting \(M\to\infty\) in (37) proves \(H_a<\infty\) almost surely from every \(r>a\).  For \(r\le a\), \(H=0\).

The Gaussian initialization has no mass on \(R_0=a\).  At a hit from outside, the martingale coefficient in (35) equals \(\sqrt{32a}>0\).  In a sufficiently small neighborhood of \(a\), its quadratic variation is strictly increasing and its drift is bounded.  The associated Brownian time change and the reflection principle show that the path cannot remain on the exterior side for any positive interval after hitting \(a\).  Hence it crosses immediately into \((0,a)\) almost surely.  Initial strict-interior paths have hitting time zero stably, while exterior paths have a finite boundary hit followed immediately by a strict-interior crossing.  Therefore the closed-ball first-hit functional is continuous at almost every limiting path.  Together with the vanishing discrete terminal jump from the characteristic lemma, the continuous mapping theorem on \([0,L]\), followed by \(L\to\infty\), yields
\[
 (\bar D_n^x,T_n^x/n)\Rightarrow(D_{\cdot\wedge H},H). \tag{38}
\]

Let \(A_n^x\) be the accepted-switch count, and let \(R_n(L)\) count rejections through
\(\lfloor nL\rfloor\wedge T_n^x\).  The covariate characteristic-and-clock lemma gives
\(R_n(L)=O_{\Pr}(\sqrt n)\).  For every \(\eta>0\),
\[
 \Pr\{(T_n^x-A_n^x)/n>\eta\}
 \le\Pr\{T_n^x>nL\}+\Pr\{R_n(L)>\eta n\}. \tag{39}
\]
For fixed \(L\), the second term tends to zero; tightness of \(T_n^x/n\) from (38) makes the first arbitrarily small by increasing \(L\).  This proves the accepted-switch/proposal-clock equivalence.

We now derive the transform of the proposal-time entrance law.  Put
\[
 A=\lambda/8>0,\qquad b=k/2-\gamma,\qquad
 U(A,b,x)=\frac1{\Gamma(A)}
 \int_0^\infty e^{-xt}t^{A-1}(1+t)^{b-A-1}\,dt. \tag{40}
\]
The integral is finite and positive.  Differentiation under the integral is justified by integrability at zero and the exponential tail.  One integration by parts then gives Kummer's equation
\[
 xU_{xx}+(b-x)U_x-AU=0. \tag{41}
\]
Define \(u_\lambda(r)=U(A,b,r/2)/U(A,b,a/2)\).  Substitution of (41) into (36) gives
\[
 \mathcal L_Ru_\lambda=\lambda u_\lambda,\qquad u_\lambda(a)=1. \tag{42}
\]
Changing variables \(z=xt\) in (40), followed by dominated convergence, gives
\(U(A,b,x)\sim x^{-A}\) as \(x\to\infty\), and hence \(u_\lambda(r)\to0\).
Ito's formula makes
\[
 e^{-\lambda(t\wedge H_a\wedge H_M)}
 u_\lambda(R_{t\wedge H_a\wedge H_M})
\]
a bounded martingale.  Let first \(t\to\infty\) and then \(M\to\infty\).  Equation (37), the almost-sure finiteness of \(H_a\), and \(u_\lambda(M)\to0\) yield
\[
 \mathbb E_r(e^{-\lambda H})=
 \begin{cases}
 1,&r\le a,\\[1mm]
 \displaystyle
 \frac{U(\lambda/8,k/2-\gamma,r/2)}
 {U(\lambda/8,k/2-\gamma,a/2)},&r>a.
 \end{cases} \tag{43}
\]
Integrating (43) against the \(\chi_k^2\) density and separating the event \(R_0\le a\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E(e^{-\lambda H})
 =F_{\chi_k^2}(a)+
 \frac{\displaystyle\int_a^\infty
 U(\lambda/8,k/2-\gamma,r/2)r^{k/2-1}e^{-r/2}\,dr}
 {\displaystyle2^{k/2}\Gamma(k/2)
 U(\lambda/8,k/2-\gamma,a/2)}. \tag{44}
\]
At \(\lambda=0\), the transform is one by definition.

The tuning dependence is strict.  Let \(\gamma_2>\gamma_1\) and let \(u_j\) be (43) for \(\gamma_j\).  The integral representation shows \(u'_2(r)<0\).  Therefore
\[
 (\mathcal L_{R,\gamma_1}-\lambda)u_2
 =16(\gamma_2-\gamma_1)u'_2<0. \tag{45}
\]
The one-dimensional maximum principle on \([a,M]\), followed by \(M\to\infty\), uses
\(u_2-u_1=0\) at \(a\) and \(u_2-u_1\to0\) at infinity to give
\(u_2(r)>u_1(r)\) for every \(r>a\).  Hence (43), and also the unconditional transform (44), is strictly increasing in finite \(\gamma\).

Finally, take a sequence in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{PSRR}}\).  The initial-score lemma gives
\[
 Z_n(W_{n,0})\Rightarrow\mathcal N_{k+1}(0,I_{k+1}). \tag{46}
\]
The actual-filtration characteristic theorem gives, on the outcome tail, limiting drift and covariance
\[
 \beta_\phi(d,e)=
 \bigl(-4d-8\gamma\phi'(\|d\|^2)d,-4e\bigr),
 \qquad c_\phi=8I_{k+1}, \tag{47}
\]
with vanishing conditional Lindeberg terms and the same discrete terminal-crossing control.  The compact-containment, tightness, Taylor expansion, and martingale-problem arguments in (29)--(34), now in dimension \(k+1\), identify the unique solution
\[
 \begin{split}
 dD_t&=\{-4D_t-8\gamma\phi'(\|D_t\|^2)D_t\}\,dt+\sqrt8\,dB_t,\\
 dE_t&=-4E_t\,dt+\sqrt8\,dB'_t.
 \end{split} \tag{48}
\]
The identity covariance in (47) and the independent Gaussian coordinates in (46) permit \(B,B'\) and \(G,\varepsilon\) to be taken mutually independent.  This independence is derived from the limiting martingale problem, not assumed of the finite-population scores.  Since the hitting argument and stopping functional depend only on \(D\), the same transfer that proved (38) gives
\[
 (\bar Z_n,T_n/n)\Rightarrow
 \left(\bigl((D_{t\wedge H}^{\mathsf T},E_{t\wedge H})^{\mathsf T}\bigr)_{t\ge0},H\right). \tag{49}
\]
Before \(H\), (48) is exactly the system in
\(\mathrm{def{:}limit\mbox{-}system}\); absorption at \(H\) proves the joint clause and its uniqueness.  No projected Markov property was used.
body.justification: The theorem gives the outcome-free covariate allocation limit and computable proposal-time first-entry law, then adds the joint outcome-residual path only on the smaller inference subclass.
body.gap: It closes the common-statistic asymptotics gap for a regular subclass of original first-entry PSRR and distinguishes its proposal and accepted clocks from stationary-chain analyses.
body.consumer: Design users can compute the asymptotic runtime transform and transport stopped statistics on the proposal or accepted-switch clock; inference users additionally obtain the joint residual process under the outcome conditions.
